correctness.rationale: PASS. For G=(Z/qZ)^n and z=r exp(iθ), direct group character sums yield λ_k=Re[(1+(q−1)z)^(n−k)(1−z)^k], multiplicity C(n,k)(q−1)^k, for all integer q>=2,n>=2 including composite q. Apart from the all-ones boundary (r=1,θ=0), factor arguments α≥0 and β≤0 have step δ=α−β<π. Their n+1 cosine arguments decrease in steps <π while straddling 0; if they all have nonnegative cosine, none can skip the full width-π negative strip, forcing nα and nβ into [−π/2,π/2]. This proves PSD exactly when r sin(θ+φ)<=sinφ and (q−1)r sin(θ−φ)<=sinφ, φ=π/(2n). Intersections of the two sine constraints yield binary two-island regime sinφ<r<=tanφ, and for q>=3 only n=2 with 1/sqrt2<r<=sqrt(1/2+1/(2(q−1)^2)). At contact n=2 the k=0,2 Fourier eigenvalues vanish and only k=1 remains, giving rank 2(q−1) and λ=q²/[2(q−1)]. Independent direct full-matrix eigenspectra for q∈{2,3,4}, n∈{2,4} in tested combinations match all algebraic levels; finite checks do not prove all parameters.
